from math import gcd


def best_average(a: list[int], k: int) -> list[int]:
    n = len(a)
    prefix = [0] * (n + 1)
    for i, x in enumerate(a):
        prefix[i + 1] = prefix[i] + x

    # Dinkelbach iteration on the current ratio p/q (exact integer arithmetic).
    # For ratio p/q, a subarray (i, j] with j - i >= k improves the ratio when
    # q * (P[j] - P[i]) - p * (j - i) > 0.
    p, q = prefix[k], k
    while True:
        best_val = 0
        best = None
        min_w = None
        min_i = -1
        for j in range(k, n + 1):
            i = j - k
            wi = q * prefix[i] - p * i
            if min_w is None or wi < min_w:
                min_w = wi
                min_i = i
            wj = q * prefix[j] - p * j
            val = wj - min_w
            if val > best_val:
                best_val = val
                best = (min_i, j)
        if best is None:
            break
        i, j = best
        p = prefix[j] - prefix[i]
        q = j - i

    g = gcd(p, q)
    return [p // g, q // g]
